speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: asked the Minister for Health following the wrong dosage of the COVID-19 vaccine for one staff at the Singapore National Eye Centre, how has the standard operating procedure been improved to ensure that such a mistake will not recur in other vaccination sites.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Health with regard to the recent vaccination overdose incident in Singapore National Eye Centre (a) why was there no dedicated staff to handle this critical operation and no formal briefing with notes if a handover was necessary; (b) whether there is a standard operating procedure (SOP) across institutions to handle vaccine preparation; and (c) how will the SOP be enhanced to prevent a recurrence.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Health how do public healthcare institutions manage the workload of medical workers to ensure that they are not overworked and made to excessively multi-task so as to avoid human errors of the type which occurred in the Singapore National Eye Centre.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: SNEC and the Ministry of Health (MOH) have followed up closely with the affected staff member, who remains well with no adverse reaction nor any side effects.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: They had been preparing and administering the vaccinations at that time.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Subsequent vaccinations for staff members were continued at the Singapore General Hospital.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: SNEC is not involved in Singapore’s vaccination exercises for any other groups.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Medical protocols are in place at all COVID-19 vaccination sites to ensure the safety of vaccinated individuals and to provide guidance on the management of the vaccination process.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Clear, written instructions on the preparation and administration of the vaccine are used.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There is a designated and segregated area for the preparation and administration of the vaccines.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There must be clear labelling to differentiate diluted and undiluted vaccine vials.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: These instructions are disseminated to and used as training materials for the staff involved in the vaccination process.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: To ensure that such lapses do not occur again, we have instructed vaccination providers to adhere strictly to the protocols.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: All vaccination providers must also undergo training to familiarise themselves with these guidelines, protocols and operational workflow prior to the commencement of their vaccination operations.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: MOH also conducts audits periodically to ensure that safety standards are adhered to.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: To ensure that each staff member in the vaccination process is assigned a manageable workload, there are specific stations within the vaccination sites for registration, screening, vaccination and monitoring.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are clearly defined roles undertaken by staff across the stations.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Staff should leave their positions only once their immediate task has been completed.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Should there be a need to step away, there must be proper documentation and handing over of roles and duties to other staff members.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The public healthcare institutions (PHIs) have planned rostered breaks and staff rotations so that staff have sufficient rest during and between their shifts.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The PHIs will also continue to train and hire more healthcare professionals, so that there will be adequate staffing to cater for these work-rest cycles and meet service demands.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Should medical workers feel over-worked or over-stretched, what recourse and remedies are available to them and how will they be assured that there will be no penalty on their performance assessments?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Job control enables workers to make decisions regarding their work and gives them more autonomy at work.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Is promoting greater job control something that the hospitals are looking into?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If members of staff at the vaccination sites are over-worked or over-stretched, they are not alone.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are staff members who are not assigned to a given station, who are available to relieve them in place and there are other staff members who are supernumerary to a given station, with a specific role of roving around and watching for incidents or the need to step in and assist.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There is also a professional domain supervising process that exists, whether you are non-clinical staff or clinical staff, whether you are nursing or medical.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: These are part of the practice of clinical medicine.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: These standard operating procedures, these are practices extended into all the vaccination sites to deliver these crisis vaccination operations.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: When it comes to the issue of autonomy and job control, in delivering these COVID-19 vaccinations as a national exercise to deal with the crisis of a pandemic, we have sub-divided the various steps into very specific tasks so that we can ensure safety, supervise the process as well as administer the vaccines to as much of our population as are going to take it up.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, there is not a lot of opportunity for autonomy and flexibility in terms of job roles, job re-creation or job re-design.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If Mr Giam is interested in these processes outside of the COVID-19 vaccination operations which is what he filed the question for, I would be happy to have a larger discussion on this matter.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I want to first declare that I am a strong advocate for the vaccination programme.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Together with the grassroots leaders of Jalan Kayu, we have been actively going out to explain and assure residents to take the vaccine, once their turn comes.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The supplementary question is to assure that the checks and balances are in place, that the safety is there for the vaccination implementation.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The vaccination centres, the places where vaccination for COVID-19 is being done, vary quite significantly, both in terms of the locale and the size, the nature of the space.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And so, the matters to be audited are going to be different.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But some of the fundamentals with respect to skill sets, the equipment, the fundamental processes and most especially, the safety of the patient are not going to change.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, the frequency and the specifics of the audits will very much depend on which sites we are talking about, what were the previous findings the last time we engaged with them and what we believe are the areas of risks.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But we are paying very close attention to all of these and the personnel at the sites, have very clearly at the top of their mind, the safety of the process.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And I am reassured by this when I go and visit them, and I have visited a number of them, the attention to detail is quite significant; they are making sure that they want to keep the process as safe as possible for Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, the nature of the audits, the details that the Member is asking, will vary quite significantly, so I do not have a clean or clear answer.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But, indeed, all the sites will be engaged in that process with MOH and our vaccine operations group.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But we will continue to pay close attention and stay in close touch with the staff.
